title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-grounded mechanism figure was available; the record remains text-only rather than publishing an unverified synthesis.

analysis.tldr: Type-aware compaction can preserve exact constraints under compression, but the closest source-fidelity control nearly ties at 50%, is absent from behavioral tests, and upstream classification cost is excluded.
analysis.problem: Uniform summarization treats safety rules, preferences, facts, and episodic logs alike even though their acceptable distortions differ.
analysis.core_idea: Classify knowledge by type, then apply per-type compaction, decomposition, or retrieval policies that pin in-scope constraints.

memory_design.write: An upstream classifier assigns each knowledge item a type.
memory_design.organize: TypeCompact preserves or rewrites by fidelity contract; TypeDecompose replicates applicable constraints across partitions.
memory_design.read: TypeRetrieve pins applicable rules before relevance-ranked items.
memory_design.update_forget: Repeated compaction is evaluated, but classification repair, deletion, and long-running audit are not.

compared_to: MaRS-FL reimplementation, the closest source-fidelity compaction operator
Type-blind LLM compactors at the same output ratio
Sonnet and hierarchical truncation on downstream behavior; MaRS-FL is missing there
analysis.evidence: On 20 configurations, TypeCompact constraint recall is .96 after five 50% rounds versus Sonnet .10. At 50/25/10%, TypeCompact is 1.00/.95/.80 and MaRS-FL .99/.75/.43. Retail pass is 37.7% versus full 28.6% and hierarchical 29.2%, but output tokens are mismatched.
analysis.why_it_matters: Compaction should expose preservation contracts and test them beside downstream behavior, not report context shrinkage alone.
limitations: The five-class classifier has kappa .45; its calls, tokens, latency, dollars, and errors are outside the deterministic operator cost.
MaRS-FL nearly ties at 50% and is not included in behavioral comparisons.
Retail context is 1,136 versus 669 tokens for baselines; worst decomposition overhead is +219%, with no energy or online maintenance audit.
